Rook Dispatch / Product School case study

What happened in Release 4.2

Dispatch shortened the time to answer and put more weight on proximity. Missed pings climbed. Every miss could lower a responder’s chances of getting the next offer.

Module 1 / Origin Story

4.2 changed the clock and the ranking

90 → 60 sec

Time to answer a ping

0.45 → 0.60

Weight on travel-time proximity

4.2 shipped on August 12, 2026. Dispatch gave nearby responders more weight and moved unanswered offers along sooner. Acceptance history’s weight fell from 0.40 to 0.25.

Module 3 / Rewind

More callouts went unaccepted

Before 4.223 / 430 · 5.3%
After 4.244 / 345 · 12.8%

The count rose by 21, and that increase was entirely in callouts involving a miss. Across the same windows, ping acceptance fell from 407/525 (77.5%) to 301/482 (62.4%), and missed pings rose from 12 to 91.

Equal 21-day windows excluding release day. Module 3 analysis and responder-week rollup

Module 4 / X-Ray Vision

A miss could make the next offer less likely

Offer expires
Acceptance score falls by 0.12
Lower score can move the responder down the next ranking

The 4.2 code applies the same 0.12 deduction to a miss and an explicit decline, with no automatic recovery. In the reconstructed callout 41245, Farlight missed and her score reached 0.00. Cindermark accepted and reached 1.00. The replay assumes scores carried through release and no unlogged updates. The ping records lack candidate ranks, travel times, and delivery timestamps, so each release change’s contribution remains uncertain.

Module 6 / Sidekicks

The checklist makes release risks visible earlier

Before approval, the skill checks for an owner, a success measure, consistent scope, and a problem statement before the proposed fix. The director brief passed after Helen was named to lead the walkthrough and report findings.

Verify
Wen checks offer order. Ravi confirms which rank and delivery events can be captured.
Rehearse
Helen tests Accept, Miss, Decline and no backup with the same candidates under both rules.
Measure
Set a first-offer-share target after a miss and regional limits for slower assignments or more unassigned callouts.

During the first trial days, Ravi reviews misses, first offers and unassigned callouts daily. Nadia brings in reports of missing or fast-expiring offers, and Marcus traces affected callouts. Agree on thresholds for pausing or expanding before launch.
